title: Eleven Weeks and One Plain Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与健康（生活与学习·健康与饮食）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与健康（生活与学习·健康与饮食）　|　核心词汇：diet　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 diet 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 the physician ① ordered a diet that no patient in the ward would have accepted, and he said the ordering was the whole of the treatment. The ② diet, meaning the food and not the regimen, ran eleven weeks and stayed unwritten on the card; a diet, he said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ diet in that ward had the same plain bowl at the side of it, and the ④ diet at the end, meaning the one they kept for the winter patients and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever repeated twice. A diet, the nurse said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to keep; the physician said the patience is the part that fills eleven weeks.

The historian meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the diet was the whole of the century, meaning the regimen and not the food. The ⑥ diet, meaning the regimen and not any of that, is the only thing in a century that everybody describes and nobody follows; diet, she said, is either something you order or the only word that means both a food and a regimen. She said the regimen is the part they remember.

By 1956 the ⑦ diet had become a line in a handbook, and the handbook had become an argument about the plain bowl. The ⑧ diet of the whole thing, the physician wrote in February, was one ward and eleven weeks of keeping; diet, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to keep. She said the keeping was never mentioned.

The ⑨ diet I remember is the one at the end, which was kept in 1968 and is still described as the plainest in the ward. A ⑩ diet, the nurse said in 1970, is the only thing that improves by being kept; every diet, she said, is a regimen that has agreed to look like a food. She said the regimen was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 饮食；膳食（指病房里规定的那一种）
B. n. 膳食（指那些食物本身，与那套养生法相对）
C. 固定搭配：order a diet 规定一种饮食
D. n. 饮食（指留给冬季病人用的那一种）
E. n. 饮食；膳食（抽象总称，指一间病房的饮食安排）
F. n. 饮食（指手册上写到、被列明的那一种）
G. n. 养生法；饮食规定（指一个世纪里被记述的那套规矩）
H. n. 养生法（抽象总称，指人人记述却无人遵行的那套）

items.q: ordered a diet that no patient in the ward would have accepted
The diet, meaning the food and not the regimen
the diet was the whole of the century
the diet had become a line in a handbook
The diet of the whole thing
A diet, the nurse said in 1970

answers.why: order a diet 意为“规定一种饮食”，1947 年医生规定了一种病房里没有一位病人肯接受的饮食。
diet 意为“膳食”，指那些食物本身而不是那套养生法，它在病历卡上挂了十一个星期而没有记录。
diet 意为“饮食、膳食”，指那间病房里每一种饮食，每一种旁边都是同一只素净的碗。
diet 意为“饮食”，指留给冬季病人用的那一种，是唯一有人重复过两次的。
diet 意为“养生法、饮食规定”，指一个世纪里被记述的那套规矩，史家说这套规矩就是那个世纪的全部。
diet 意为“养生法”，指人人记述却无人遵行的那套而不是那些食物，是世纪里人人都记述、却无人遵行的东西。
diet 意为“饮食”，指手册上写到、被列明的那一种，到 1956 年这种饮食成了手册里的一行。
diet 意为“饮食、膳食”，医生二月写道，整件事的膳食是一间病房和十一个星期的坚持。
diet 意为“饮食”，我记得的是末尾那一种，1968 年坚持下来，至今仍被说成病房里最素的一种。
diet 为抽象总称，护士 1970 年说，一种饮食是唯一会因为被坚持下来而变得更好的东西。
